sources: Parks Australia, Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, Thorny devil: a small dragon covered in densely packed spikes; unusual rocking walk thought to confuse birds of prey; knob-like 'false head' on its shoulders; can puff itself up when threatened; eats only ants, parks beside an ant trail; a single devil can eat thousands of ants in a day; standing in a puddle or wet sand, water runs up its legs and over its body to its mouth via narrow grooves between scales; pale yellow and red in warm weather, darker when cold or alarmed; https://uluru.gov.au/discover/nature/animals/thorny-devil

University of Western Australia news, 'Flat out lizard drinking: thorny devil's remarkable desert survival' (2016; Prof. P. Withers): drinks from puddles via skin capillary channels between overlapping scales that lead to the mouth; flicks moist sand onto its back to absorb some moisture; about a pinhead of water per gulp; condensation from humid air is not enough to drink; https://news.uwa.edu.au/201611039172/research/flat-out-lizard-drinking-thorny-devils-remarkable-desert-survival

Comanns P., Withers P.C., Esser F.J., Baumgartner W. (2016) 'Cutaneous water collection by a moisture-harvesting lizard, the thorny devil (Moloch horridus)', Journal of Experimental Biology 219:3473-3479: lizards standing in water fill their skin capillary system and drink from it; rain and moist sand are likely regular water sources; https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.151407

PBS Nature, 'Featured Creature: Thorny Devil': the neck knob is a false head meant to deceive predators; when threatened it curls its real head between its front legs; eats mainly ants, estimated 600 to 2500 per meal; https://www.pbs.org/wnet/nature/blog/inside-nature-featured-creature-thorny-devil

title: This Lizard Drinks Water Through Its Feet 🦎

beats.say: This lizard drinks with its feet. Water runs up its legs, and into its mouth.
So I shrank myself to lizard size, and went to the Australian desert.
The thorny devil. A small dragon, covered in spikes.
After a rain, it steps into a puddle.
Its skin is full of tiny grooves between the scales.
The water creeps up those grooves, over its body, all the way to its mouth.
Then it gulps. About a pinhead of water per sip.
It even flicks wet sand onto its own back to wet its skin even more.
Here's the weird part. It has two heads. Sort of.
On its shoulders is a spiky knob that looks like a head.
When something attacks, it tucks its real head down between its front legs.
So the hunter is looking at the fake head instead.
It can also puff itself up to look bigger.
And it walks with a strange rocking motion, to confuse hungry birds.
It eats one thing. Ants.
It parks next to an ant trail, and snaps them up, one by one.
Thousands of ants, in a single day.
Would you hold one?
A spiky dragon with a spare head, sipping water through its feet.
Follow me. Next, the spider whose silk was strung inside wartime bombsights.
